- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates drop; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to overcorrect downward; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven volatility; if sentiment swings sharply, reduce forecast volatility by 20–40% relative to historical range.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.2–0.5), model tends to average out; avoid overfitting to recent history; use 10–15 day smoothing for sentiment-weighted adjustments.
